title: Apple Sets Pre‑Order Countdown: iPhone Duo Ready for Order Soon – MacRumors Report
body:
Apple has set a strict deadline for consumers who want to secure a spot in the upcoming iPhone Duo pre‑order queue, giving shoppers until 9 p.m. Pacific Time today to complete the “Get Ready” step on the company’s website or Apple Store app. The move, announced early this morning, signals Apple’s intent to streamline the high‑volume launch process and ensure that only seriously interested customers move forward to the actual ordering phase, which is expected to open later this week.

The “Get Ready” requirement is essentially a pre‑registration that captures a customer’s shipping address, payment information and device preferences before the official pre‑order window opens. By completing this step, users will receive a notification when the pre‑order begins, along with a unique link that bypasses the general queue. Apple has framed the deadline as a way to “reduce friction” for buyers and to mitigate the server overloads that have plagued previous launches, such as the iPhone 14 and the much‑anticipated Apple Vision Pro. Those who miss the cutoff will still be able to purchase the iPhone Duo after the initial wave, but they may face longer wait times and limited inventory.

Industry analysts see the deadline as part of Apple’s broader strategy to manage demand for what is expected to be its most innovative smartphone to date. The iPhone Duo, rumored to feature a dual‑screen design and advanced AI‑driven photography capabilities, has generated significant buzz across tech forums and social media platforms. By filtering out casual browsers, Apple can allocate server capacity and customer‑service resources more efficiently, potentially avoiding the “waiting‑room” fiascos that have marred past releases. Moreover, the pre‑registration data gives Apple a clearer picture of geographic demand, allowing the company to fine‑tune its logistics and shipping plans ahead of the full rollout.

Consumers have responded with a mix of enthusiasm and urgency. Early‑bird fans have already flooded Apple’s online portals, reporting that the “Get Ready” interface is straightforward: users simply log in with their Apple ID, confirm their preferred model and storage configuration, and verify payment details. Apple’s support channels have been bolstered with additional chat agents to handle the surge, and the company has warned that the system will close automatically at the 9 p.m. deadline, after which no further entries will be accepted for the first pre‑order batch. Retail analysts caution that the limited window could create a sense of scarcity that drives early sales, but it also risks alienating customers who encounter technical glitches or who are in different time zones.

The timing of the deadline also aligns with Apple’s typical launch cadence. Historically, the tech giant opens pre‑orders a few days after announcing a new device, with the first shipments arriving roughly a week later. By setting a firm cut‑off for the preparatory step, Apple can synchronize its supply chain, ensuring that the initial batch of iPhone Duo units reaches eager buyers without delay. Supply‑chain experts note that Apple’s manufacturing partners, primarily based in China and India, have already ramped up production, and the pre‑order data will help calibrate final assembly volumes to avoid overproduction.

Looking ahead, the iPhone Duo’s official pre‑order launch is expected to commence later this week, with the first shipments slated for early next month. The success of the “Get Ready” initiative will likely influence how Apple structures future product rollouts, especially as the company expands its portfolio into foldable and dual‑display devices. For now, customers who have secured their spot can anticipate a smoother purchasing experience, while those who missed the deadline will need to monitor Apple’s channels for the next wave of availability. As the tech world watches, the iPhone Duo could set a new benchmark for how premium smartphones are introduced to a global market.
